title: Q1. Gas Station Circuit
statement:
There are n gas stations on a circular route. gas[i] is available at station i and cost[i] is needed to travel to station (i + 1) modulo n. Find the starting station index for one complete trip, or print -1. Indices are zero-based.

Input: n, then gas and cost arrays.
Output: the starting index or -1.

title: Q2. Spiral Traversal of a Matrix
statement:
Given an m x n matrix, print its values in spiral order: top row, right column, bottom row reversed, left column reversed, repeating inward.

Input: m n followed by the matrix.
Output: the traversal separated by spaces.

title: Q3. Bitwise Rules for Two Matrices
statement:
For two n x n matrices A and B, build C: if i < j use bitwise OR, if i == j use AND, and if i > j use XOR.

Input: n, matrix A, then matrix B.
Output: matrix C.

title: Q4. Rotate a Matrix 90 Degrees Clockwise
statement: Given an n x n matrix, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise and print the result.

title: Q5. Rotate Each Row Right by K
statement: Given an N x M matrix and K, rotate every row to the right by K positions. Use K modulo M.

title: Q6. Upper and Lower Triangular Sums
statement: Given an n x n matrix, print the sum of elements on and above the main diagonal, followed by the sum of elements on and below it.

title: Q7. Zigzag Row Traversal
statement: Print alternate matrix rows in opposite directions: row 0 left to right, row 1 right to left, and so on.

title: Q8. Rotate a Matrix 90 Degrees Anticlockwise
statement: Given an n x n matrix, rotate it 90 degrees anticlockwise and print the result.

title: Q9. Sum of Boundary Elements
statement: Given an n x m matrix, find the sum of all boundary elements. Count each corner only once.

title: Q10. Sum of Both Diagonals
statement: Given an n x n matrix, print the sum of both diagonals. In an odd-sized matrix, count the center element only once.
